title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 577-629, section VI 'Les groupes M_{rho,sigma} généraux : récapitulation, raffinement'). The data are a profinite group G (fraktur), a surjection GL(2,Z)^ -> G, and the images rho, sigma, tau of the standard generators of the profinite completion of GL(2,Z): rho and sigma are torsion elements of SL(2,Z), and tau is a reflection of determinant -1. G^+ is the image of SL(2,Z)^. The previous page adds an open subgroup G^q of G^+, normal in G^+. It lets one cut down the big group M (of which Gamma_Q^~ = M/G^+ is a quotient, a Grothendieck-Teichmüller-type group) to the subgroup M^q of elements that normalize G^q and act trivially on G^+/G^q. Its image Gamma_Q^{q~} is open, and its representations can be studied.

This page does three things.
(1) It proposes a second interesting family of examples: G = the group of integral adelic points H(Z^) = prod_p H(Z_p) of a group scheme H over Z, receiving GL(2,Z)^. Grothendieck notes that rho, sigma, tau then need not generate G topologically; they may generate it only 'modulo a finite group', i.e. only an open subgroup. In that case the constructions should be 'paraphrased in the schematic case', and he says he will come back to this. A natural choice of G^q is then inside the neutral component of G (presumably H^0(Z^)).
(2) A notational decision: he will not write Z^G_{rho,sigma}, M^G_{rho,sigma}. He keeps the simpler symbols Z_{rho,sigma}, M_{rho,sigma}, with the understanding that they depend on the chosen G^q.
(3) Definition (3): G^q_tau = M_tau . G^q = {1,tau} . G^q, a subgroup of G. This is the 'τ-extended' version of G^q. It is what is used on the next page in the definition of Z_{rho,sigma}, a subgroup of Aut(G^+) x Z^* x mu x mu. There, the conditions u(rho) = alpha(rho) and u(sigma) = beta(sigma) are imposed with alpha, beta in G^q_tau, carrying a sign epsilon_G(alpha) = ±1 according to whether the τ-component is present.

The overall aim is a family of 'relative' or 'level-q' variants of the GT-type groups attached to quotients of GL(2,Z)^, including congruence-type (adelic) quotients.
errors: {1,tau}.G^q is a subgroup only if tau normalizes G^q. The previous page only assumes G^q is invariant in G^+, so tau-stability of G^q is an implicit extra hypothesis.

The claim that rho, sigma, tau generate an open subgroup ('modulo groupe fini') of H(Z^) is not automatic. For H = GL_2 the closure of the image of GL(2,Z) is {g in GL_2(Z^) : det g = ±1}, which has infinite index (Z^*/{±1} is infinite). For semisimple H the closure of an arithmetic image is open (all of it under strong approximation in the simply connected case, finite index otherwise). So some hypothesis (semisimplicity, or a determinant/centre condition) is tacitly needed. Grothendieck hedges with 'peut-être'.
Also implicit: the definition of 'surjection GL(2,Z)^ -> G' must be relaxed to 'homomorphism with open image' in the adelic case. He acknowledges this and defers it ('J'y reviendrai').

ideas.what: Taking as quotient target of GL(2,Z)^ the integral adelic points of a group scheme over Z (congruence-type quotients), with rho, sigma, tau generating only an open subgroup, and suggesting a 'schematic' rewriting of the constructions
ideas.modern_name: congruence completion / adelic images of the modular group; relative or arithmetic completions of SL_2(Z); Galois action on congruence quotients of pi_1(M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Congruence completion: classical (Serre, Melnikov on the congruence kernel). Relative completion of modular groups: Hain (1997), Hain-Matsumoto (2000s).
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or Longue Marche to my knowledge; unsure

ideas.what: Restricting to an open normal level subgroup G^q of G^+, with a preferred choice inside the neutral component of the group scheme
ideas.modern_name: level structures / finite-index variants of GT-type groups (e.g. GT acting on finite-level modular towers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various (Ihara, Nakamura, Hain-Matsumoto for level structures)

ideas.what: Definition G^q_tau = {1,tau}.G^q, the subgroup used to define Z_{rho,sigma} with sign character epsilon
ideas.modern_name: orientation-reversing extension of a level subgroup

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans to paraphrase his GT-type groups M_{rho,sigma} 'in the schematic case', where the target is a group scheme over Z and G is its adelic integral points. This anticipates replacing profinite quotients of GL(2,Z)^ by algebraic group targets, close in spirit to relative/weighted completion of the modular group. The deferred 'J'y reviendrai' thread is not known to have been carried out by him.
missed.quote: il faudrait plutôt paraphraser les constructions qui suivent dans le cas schématique. J'y reviendrai par la suite.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A version of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller formalism with congruence/adelic group-scheme targets connects to Hain-Matsumoto relative completion and to the study of Galois/GT actions on modular-curve towers. Checking whether his later pages develop it could show an early independent route to these ideas.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly bookkeeping: a notational decision and the definition of G^q_tau. The one forward-looking remark (adelic group-scheme targets, a 'schematic' version of the constructions) is suggestive of later relative-completion work, but it is only sketched and deferred.
transcription_corrections: 'Mais choix [?] intéressant' should read 'Un choix intéressant'.
'n'engendrent pas [?] 𝔊^* que modulo groupe fini' is more likely 'n'engendrent peut-être 𝔊^+ (or 𝔊) que modulo groupe fini'; the superscript looks like '+' rather than '*'.
'pts adéliques entiers' is correct, with 'entiers' added above the line.
Page is archive p. 651 (manuscript page number not visible; it sits between ms. pp. 628 and 629).
In the next page's transcription, 'G^φ' should be read as G^q (the same superscript q).
